14 A uniform cylinder of weight 25.0 N is suspended from a newton meter.
The cylinder is fully submerged in water, as shown.
The reading on the newton meter is 10.0 N.
newton
meter
cylinder
water
The water is replaced by a liquid with a density 10% greater than the density of water. The
cylinder remains fully submerged.
What is the new reading on the newton meter?
A
8.5 N
B
9.0 N
C
11.0 N
D
11.5 N

hints: Notice the meter reads $10.0 \text{ N}$ while the true weight is $25.0 \text{ N}$ - the $15.0 \text{ N}$ difference is the upthrust in water.
Recall upthrust equals weight of displaced fluid, $U = \rho V g$, so for the same fully submerged cylinder $U$ is proportional to liquid density.
A liquid 10% denser gives upthrust $1.10$ times larger - work out the new upthrust then subtract it from $25.0 \text{ N}$.
walkthrough: Identify forces on the stationary cylinder: weight $W = 25.0 \text{ N}$ down, upthrust $U$ up, and tension $T$ up shown by the newton meter.
In water, equilibrium gives $T + U = W$, so $U_{water} = W - T = 25.0 - 10.0 = 15.0 \text{ N}$.
For a fully submerged body, $U = \rho V g$ with the same $V$ and $g$, so $U$ scales directly with liquid density $\rho$.
New density is 10% greater, so $U_{new} = 1.10 \times U_{water} = 1.10 \times 15.0 = 16.5 \text{ N}$.
New meter reading is the new tension: $T_{new} = W - U_{new} = 25.0 - 16.5 = 8.5 \text{ N}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Upthrust rises to $16.5 \text{ N}$, so reading is $25.0 - 16.5 = 8.5 \text{ N}$.

B.explanation: This subtracts 10% of the $10.0 \text{ N}$ reading instead of adding 10% to the $15.0 \text{ N}$ upthrust.

C.explanation: This adds 10% to the $10.0 \text{ N}$ meter reading instead of to the upthrust force.

D.explanation: This adds 10% of the $15.0 \text{ N}$ upthrust to the $10.0 \text{ N}$ reading, but greater upthrust must lower the reading.
